subject.title: refactor(prompt): use plain inbound context labels and drop system-tag sanitizer

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the provenance-marker contract and Doctor-only repair path as the canonical boundary for all inbound prompt context, including the stated residual risk for installs that skip Doctor repair?
rationale: This is a deliberate security and compatibility policy choice spanning core prompt boundaries, plugin SDK aliases, stored transcripts, and memory recall; source review can verify the mechanism but cannot decide the acceptable upgrade and trust-boundary tradeoff.

options.title: Approve the canonical marker boundary
options.body: Rebase and land after current-main upgrade proof confirms the marker, deprecated aliases, transcript rewrite, and LanceDB purge remain coherent.

options.title: Keep the old label contract for now
options.body: Pause the refactor and retain the existing sanitizer and label scheme until owners choose a narrower migration plan.

options.title: Split the migration from the label refactor
options.body: Land only the bounded security-boundary repair after separating SDK and persisted-state migration decisions into reviewable follow-up work.

recommendation.title: Approve the canonical marker boundary
recommendation.body: Rebase and land after current-main upgrade proof confirms the marker, deprecated aliases, transcript rewrite, and LanceDB purge remain coherent.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the current implementation context and can route the required maintainer decision to the relevant prompt-security and plugin-SDK reviewers.
